sentences: Your drive isn't full, so what's maxed out?
It's how much of the time your drive was busy.
It says nothing about free space.
A hard drive reads one scattered spot at a time.
Its arm swings to the right track, then waits for the platter to spin the data underneath.
It manages only about 75 to 100 random reads per second.
When startup apps all want files at once, the line never empties.
It answers in well under a millisecond, so the same work barely registers.
Find the real culprit in our video, Why Your PC Is Slow.
